title: Trace patterns for multi-model fanout and routing
content:
Purpose:
This note captures proposed tracing and dashboarding patterns for requests that fan out to multiple model variants or backends (multi-model routing, polyglot model stacks, cascade/pipeline inference). It focuses on making timing, cost attribution, and decision points visible so we can: triage latency/cost regressions, root-cause incorrect fallback behavior, and validate routing policies in production.

Context / why this is hard:
- A single user request may spawn multiple concurrent or sequential model calls (e.g., small fast LM for parsing, larger LM for generation, reranker, safety checker). Observability must show the overall request story and per-model contribution.
- Routing decisions (region/capacity/fallback to lower-tier models) are often made by policy engines; without clear span annotations we lose the decision context.
- Cost attribution requires per-span token counts + model variant metadata.
- High-cardinality model metadata (quantization, shard id, GPU type) must be surfaced carefully to avoid explosion in dashboards/alerts.

Goals (non-technical):
- Make total end-to-end latency and percent contribution per model easy to query.
- Show which routing rule fired and why (capacity, SLO, cost-trigger, blacklist).
- Provide a compact dashboard for day-to-day ops and a detailed trace view for deep dive.
- Keep dashboards low-cardinality; push high-cardinality attributes to trace UI only (linked when needed).

Span & trace conventions (proposal):
1) Trace root: request_received
   - tags: request_id (global UUID), customer_id, route, requested_model_profile, client_sdk_version

2) Routing span: route_decision (child of root, short-lived)
   - tags: routing_policy_id, decision (serve | fallback | queue | reject), rationale (capacity|cost|blacklist|version-pin), fallback_chain_index (0..n)
   - Add sampling tag: route_experiment_variant if A/B rollout in effect

3) Per-model invocation: model_call (one per call, can be parallel)
   - Tags: model_name, model_version, quantization_profile, compute_tier (hosted|dedicated|private), node_type (a100-v4|t4|cpu-small), gpu_shard_id (if applicable), token_input_count, token_output_count, prompt_prefix_cached (true|false)
   - Metrics emitted attached to span: model_infer_time_ms, model_load_time_ms (if warmup), model_gpu_mem_mb, model_gpu_util_pct

4) Post-processing spans: reranker, prompt_transform, safety_check, response_builder (each annotated with tool name and brief counters)

5) Error and fallback annotations:
   - For any model_call that triggers a fallback, attach span tag fallback_to (model_name:version) and fallback_reason (timeout|oom|bad_output|traceback)
   - Attach representative error message truncated to 256 chars in span tag error_snippet for quick inspection

Sampling strategy and cardinality guidance:
- Always sample 100% of route_decision spans as they are small and low-cardinality. Route_decision contains the experiment/decision info we need.
- Sample 10% of full traces that include model_call spans for long-running customers; increase to 100% for customers in postmortems or active experiments.
- For high-traffic public endpoints, always sample model_call spans at 1% by default, but force-sample any trace where model_infer_time_ms > threshold (e.g., 95th p95 SLA) or token_output_count > predefined limit.
- Avoid indexing model metadata like gpu_shard_id or quantization_profile in dashboards; use trace UI to inspect when investigating. Only index model_name, model_version (coarse), compute_tier for dashboards.

Dashboard surface (compact + drilldown):
A) Compact Ops Dashboard (low-cardinality panels):
   - E2E latency distribution (p50/p90/p95/p99) by route
   - Model contribution heatmap: fraction of E2E latency attributable to top N model_calls (derived metric: per-span time / root duration)
   - Routing decision split: % serve vs fallback vs queue vs reject over time
   - Cost-rate panel: token/sec and estimated cost/sec (approximate using model_name->cost_multiplier)
   - Top 10 customers by request volume + their mean E2E latency

B) Drilldown Dashboard (linked from compact panels):
   - Trace-sampled waterfall view aggregated: average span timings for model_call and route_decision
   - Slow traces table with quick-links to full trace explorer, with columns: request_id, route, decision, root_latency_ms, model_names involved, token_counts
   - Fallback incidents list: count by fallback_reason and top affected routes

C) Debug widget for experiments: when route_experiment_variant present, show variant comparison for latency/cost/quality (quality metrics fed in from evaluation pipeline).

Alerting recommendations:
- Alert on routing-flap: sudden jump in % of fallbacks for a route (>5% absolute increase in 5 min window)
- Alert on model regressed p95 inference time crossing SLO for more than 10 minutes
- Alert on model_call error rate > X% of calls for a model (configurable per model)

Quick runbook snippets (triage flow):
1) Compact dashboard shows increased E2E p95 for route "chat:general"
   - Open slow traces table -> filter request_ids with route==chat:general and p95 threshold -> inspect route_decision tags to see if fallback frequency increased.
   - If fallback_reason == timeout, inspect model_call spans for model_infer_time_ms and node_type; correlate with node-level GPU saturation metrics in infra dashboard.
   - If fallback_reason == bad_output, link to evaluation job (linked_artifacts) and surface sample inputs/outputs for QA.

2) Model-specific slowdowns
   - Compare model_call p95 vs historical baseline; check if model_version or quantization_profile changed recently (use linked_artifacts to find rollout PR).
   - If new model_version is suspected, escalate to rollout owner and consider immediate rollback.

Open questions / tradeoffs:
- How much metadata do we index in metrics vs keep purely in traces? Recommendation: index compute_tier and model_name:coarse only. Keep gpu_shard_id, quantization_profile, and prompt_prefix_cached only in traces.
- Token accounting: we currently only have token counts emitted post-hoc from runtime. Should we move token counter to span-level metric to reduce skepticism when cost alerts fire? Pros: immediate attribution. Cons: higher cardinality and ingestion cost.

Next steps (proposed):
1) Iterate on a lightweight instrumentation library patch that ensures route_decision and model_call spans conform to tags above. PR: github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/889 (linked).
2) Build compact ops dashboard panels (low-cardinality) and validate with two busy routes for 2 weeks.
3) Run an experiment to sample 100% of traces for a subset of customers for 48h to validate tag coverage and surface missing fields.

Notes to self / TODOs:
- Add example trace JSON snippet to confluence page CONFLUENCE-OBS-4321 (blocked on instrumentation PR).
- Coordinate with Platform Eng for GPU tagging convention (node_type canonicalization).

Appendix: short example span checklist (for engineers adding spans)
- Does the root include request_id and route?
- Does route_decision include routing_policy_id and rationale?
- Does every model_call include model_name, model_version, token counts, and model_infer_time_ms metric?
- Add fallback tags when relevant (fallback_to, fallback_reason).

End.
